title: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM)
everyday_terms: sudden death in a young relative
summary: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy makes the heart muscle thicker than usual, which can make it harder for the heart to pump. Many people have mild or no symptoms; some have chest pain, breathlessness or an irregular heartbeat.
inheritance_plain: It is inherited in an autosomal dominant way: one changed copy of one of the genes linked to it (most often MYBPC3 or MYH7) can be enough to cause it. A parent with the change can pass it on, and the chance is the same for each pregnancy. A genetic counsellor talks this through with you.
carrier_meaning: For a dominant condition, one changed copy can be enough to cause it, so people with a change are not usually called carriers. How much it affects someone varies, and some people have few signs for many years. A genetic counsellor explains what a result means.
disease_meaning: People with HCM are looked after by heart specialists, who check the heart regularly and offer treatment when needed. Close relatives can be offered heart checks.
screening: A heart scan and ECG can check the heart, and a genetic test can look for a change in the genes linked to HCM. A genetic counsellor can explain which relatives might choose to be checked.
suggested_questions: Someone in my family has HCM. What could that mean for me?
What does a test for HCM involve?
card_summary: The heart muscle is thicker than usual. Heart specialists check and treat it.
carrier_short: One changed copy. Can be enough to cause the condition. A counsellor explains.
disease_short: Thicker heart muscle; regular checks and treatment from heart specialists.
care: Specialist heart and inherited cardiac conditions clinics, genetic counselling and family support groups.
